title: Muslim League declares a programme of direct action
detail: After the collapse of agreement around the Cabinet Mission framework, the Muslim League resolved to abandon reliance on constitutional negotiation alone and declared 16 August as Direct Action Day.

title: Hartal and rally in Calcutta escalate into violence
detail: In Bengal the League ministry backed a public holiday and a major rally in Calcutta. Street confrontations, forced closures, retaliatory mobilization, and inflammatory political atmosphere quickly turned the day into organized communal bloodshed.

title: The Great Calcutta Killing devastates the city
detail: For several days Calcutta experienced killings, arson, looting, and reprisals between Hindus and Muslims on a massive scale, while administrative response and political responsibility became deeply contested.

title: Violence spreads to Noakhali, Bihar, and beyond
detail: The Calcutta killings became both precedent and provocation for further communal massacres elsewhere, deepening the sense that coexistence under a united constitutional future was collapsing.

title: Partition of Bengal becomes more likely
detail: Direct Action Day and its aftermath hardened political positions in Bengal and across India, helping make the final partition settlement of 1947 appear increasingly unavoidable.
